title: Over 400 Flights Delayed and 15 Diverted as Monsoon Downpour Paralyses Delhi Airport
excerpt: Heavy rain, thunderstorms, and 30-40 kmph winds disrupt operations at India's busiest airport; airlines issue travel advisories as waterlogging chokes road access across Delhi-NCR
body:
• At least 15 flights were diverted and over 280 delayed at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport on Monday as heavy rain and thunderstorms battered the national capital
  • IndiGo, Air India, and SpiceJet issued travel advisories urging passengers to check flight status before heading to the airport
  • Diversions were routed to Jaipur, Chandigarh, and Lucknow due to poor visibility and water accumulation on runways
  • Gurugram authorities issued a work-from-home advisory for Tuesday as waterlogging and traffic chaos persisted across the NCR

Heavy monsoon rain and violent thunderstorms paralysed flight operations at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGIA) on Monday, forcing the diversion of at least 15 flights and delaying hundreds more across India's busiest aviation hub.

According to data from flight tracking website Flightradar24, over 280 services were delayed and more than 20 flights were cancelled at the airport, which handles roughly 1,300 flight movements daily. Reports from later in the day put the total number of delayed flights closer to 400, with 26 cancellations, as disruptions cascaded through the evening schedule.

Diversions and Airline Advisories

Airport officials confirmed that 12 flights were diverted to Jaipur, two to Chandigarh, and one to Lucknow after poor visibility, thunderstorm activity, and water accumulation on runways made landing conditions unsafe at IGIA.

"Adverse weather conditions may impact flight operations to and from Delhi today."

— Air India, in a post on X

IndiGo said bad weather had impacted flight schedules and that the airline was closely monitoring conditions. The carrier apologised for the inconvenience and began rebooking passengers on next available flights. SpiceJet announced hotel vouchers for passengers stranded beyond six hours and urged travellers to check their flight status online before heading to the airport.

Air India coordinated with the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) to minimise disruption to connecting journeys, while the DGCA issued a circular advising airlines to factor in additional turnaround time and thoroughly check runway surface conditions before resuming operations.

Waterlogging Chokes Road Access to Airport

The flight disruptions were compounded by severe waterlogging and traffic gridlocks across Delhi-NCR that made reaching the airport a challenge in itself. Key stretches including Mathura Road, NH-24, and the Delhi-Noida Direct Flyway witnessed traffic jams lasting over two hours. Several underpasses, including those at ITO, Rajghat, and near AIIMS, were waterlogged up to three feet.

The Delhi Traffic Police issued multiple advisories urging residents to avoid non-essential travel and use the Delhi Metro. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi deployed over 200 pumps to clear stagnant water, though the intensity of rainfall overwhelmed drainage systems in several zones.

Winds, Power Outages Compound Disruption

Winds of 30-40 kmph accompanied the downpour, uprooting trees and snapping electricity poles across South and West Delhi. Residents of Malviya Nagar, Vasant Kunj, Dwarka, and parts of Gurugram reported power outages lasting up to two hours. The Delhi Disaster Management Authority activated its control room and urged citizens to stay indoors.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) maintained its weather alert, forecasting that the monsoon trough would remain active with light to moderate rain expected through mid-week.

What It Means for NRI Travellers

The disruptions are a reminder of the monsoon-season risks that frequently affect India's air travel infrastructure during August and September. NRIs planning trips to Delhi or transiting through IGIA should build extra buffer time into their itineraries and consider travel insurance that covers weather-related delays. Passengers on connecting flights through Delhi are particularly vulnerable, as cascading delays can cause missed connections on both domestic and international legs.

Airlines recommend checking flight status through their respective apps and websites before departing for the airport, and allowing extra commute time due to waterlogged roads.

Gurugram Issues Work-From-Home Advisory

Following Monday's deluge, Gurugram authorities issued a work-from-home advisory for all corporate offices and educational institutions on Tuesday, citing persistent waterlogging and traffic congestion. Delhi is expected to see another spell of rain and thunderstorms on Tuesday, though intensity is expected to decrease.

Airport operations were gradually restored by Monday evening, though several inbound flights continued to face delays past sunset. The IMD's extended forecast suggests the monsoon trough will remain active over northwest India for the next 48 hours.
